label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
**Date:** November 11, 2026

**To:** Mrs. Okafor
**From:** [Your Full Name], School Bus Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
**Subject:** Statement regarding the afternoon pickup on Tuesday, October 27, 2026

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

Thank you for taking the time to share your concerns with the transportation office. I know that afternoon was frightening for you, and I'm sorry it was such a hard day for you and for Amara. I want you to know I take the safety of every child on my bus seriously, and I have driven Amara every day since the start of the year. I'm glad to keep driving her, and I want to make sure we can both get past this.

I'm writing to explain what happened from my side, as my supervisor, Darlene, asked me to do. I've tried to stick to what I observed and what I was required to do. I'm not writing this to blame you. I understand that you were worried, and I would probably feel the same way if I were in your place. I have grandchildren of my own.

**What happened**

On Tuesday, October 27, I was running the afternoon route for Route 9 with Bus 41. Our scheduled arrival at the Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street stop was 3:50 p.m. I arrived at approximately 3:52 p.m. Amara was on my bus that afternoon. Her backpack has the green tag, which tells me that an adult must be present at the stop to receive her.

I waited at the stop from about 3:52 until roughly 3:55 p.m. I looked up and down the corner and I did not see an adult waiting for her or anyone who appeared to be there for her. I did not see you, and I did not see a vehicle with a person standing beside it. There was a box truck parked on the side of Brandt Street where I could see, which may have blocked the view from the bus, but I want to be clear that I did not see you wave or signal to me.

Under the district's rule for kindergarten riders, when no adult is present at the stop, the student stays on the bus and returns to the school. The school office is then notified so they can contact the parent or guardian. That is what I was required to do, so I followed it.

At 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch contacted Fairmont Elementary. I still had three more stops and fourteen other students on the bus, so I could not leave the bus to walk across the road or check the other side of the street. I have a responsibility to all fourteen of those children, and leaving them on the bus unattended was not an option for me.

I brought Amara back to Fairmont Elementary, arriving at approximately 4:31 p.m. I walked her into the office and handed her directly to Mrs. Petrakis.

**How Amara was during the ride**

Amara was calm for the entire ride. She was coloring on her folder and was not upset. At one point she asked whether she could keep riding the bus. I told her we were taking a little extra trip to get her back to school, and I tried to keep her comfortable and occupied until we arrived.

**Regarding your concerns**

You wrote that I "drove off laughing." I was not laughing. When we pulled away from the stop, a fourth grader in seat 2 was out of his seat, and I was telling him to sit back down for his safety and the safety of the other riders. I understand that from a distance, someone could have seen my face or heard my voice and interpreted it differently, but I was not laughing at Amara or at the situation.

You also wrote that I "took" Amara. I want to explain that I did not take her anywhere she was not supposed to be. Under the policy I was required to follow, she was returned to her school, where she was supposed to be when no adult was available to receive her at the stop.

I also want to be honest that this has happened once before on my route, several years ago, with a different family. In that case, the parents thanked me for following the procedure once they understood the situation. I hope that once you have the full picture, you can see that I was trying to keep Amara safe under the rules we are all asked to follow.

**Requests**

I respectfully request that the transportation office pull the camera footage from Bus 41 for Tuesday, October 27, from approximately 3:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. The camera should show the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, the arrival time, and whether an adult was present. I believe this footage will help clarify what I saw and when.

For future afternoons, I would ask that if you are picking Amara up, you stand on the same side of the street as the bus, or step out of your vehicle where I can see you. That way I can clearly see that an adult is there to receive her before I open the door. If you have a different arrangement for her pickup, please let the school and transportation office know so the information is on file.

**Closing**

I did not follow the policy because I wanted to upset you. I followed it because it is the rule for kindergarten riders with green tags, and it was the only way I could keep Amara safe with fourteen other children still on my bus. I am sorry that the afternoon was difficult for you. I am not sorry for following the rule, but I do regret that you felt left out of the process, and I want us to work together so this does not happen again.

I have driven this route for 28 years with no written complaints or disciplinary actions on my record, and I take that responsibility seriously. I'm glad to keep driving Amara. If there is anything else you would like me to clarify, or if you would like to meet with the transportation office, I am willing to do that.

Thank you for your time and for reading this.

Sincerely,

[Your Full Name]
School Bus Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
[Your Phone Number, if you want it included]

---

Before you send it, check that the times, the bus number, and the names match what you wrote down that day. You may also want to remove the line about the previous incident if you'd rather keep the statement focused on this one event. Your statement is due Friday, November 13, so you have time to review it with Darlene before it goes in.
